English: Wooden Steppe Shrine
A simple wooden shrine, decorated with carved totems and idols, offering a focal point for worship and gatherings.
Grassy Knoll Altar
A humble, makeshift altar raised atop a gentle knoll, marked by stones and offerings to the spirits of the steppe.
Stone Steppe Altar
A sturdy altar of hewn stone, surrounded by sacred markers, providing a lasting place for rites and offerings.
Turf Sanctuary
A broad earthen mound with a partially sheltered altar, where the faithful gather for larger ceremonies beneath the open sky.
Steppe Prayer Shelter
A timber-framed shelter with earthen walls, offering protection from the elements for prayer and council. Adorned with sacred banners and relics.
Steppe Gathering Circle
A great ring of standing stones encircling a central altar, used for seasonal festivals, judgments, and assemblies of the faithful.
Enclosed Steppe Shrine
A walled and roofed sanctuary with stone foundations, protecting relics and hosting learned priests who instruct followers in the faith.
Raised Steppe Altar
A monumental stone platform, towering above the grasslands, visible for miles and drawing pilgrims from near and far to worship and give homage.
Steppe Pilgrims Hall
An expansive complex of halls and courtyards, offering shelter, food, and teaching to pilgrims and novices traveling the sacred steppe routes.
Grand Steppe Sanctuary
A vast walled sanctuary, crowned by an ornate temple and ringed by towers, the spiritual heart of the steppe and a beacon for all the faithful.
